page: OVHcloud bm-s1 is a bare metal virtualized server in the Metal product family operating under the KVM hypervisor. The system provides 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs configured at a base frequency of 4.0 GHz. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, and carries 1920 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The network interface supports a baseline throughput of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs present.

Hardware capabilities highlight a strong memory footprint and high single-core base clock rates alongside fast local solid-state capacity. With an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, it satisfies workloads requiring large working memory buffers alongside persistent high-throughput local disk storage. The 1920 GB NVMe volume delivers direct low-latency I/O without the operational latency of network block devices, although the setup provides standard 1 Gbps networking which may constrain cross-node replication bandwidth under heavy transfers.

The configuration provides cost-efficient access to dedicated CPU cycles paired with substantial RAM and fast internal NVMe storage in an entry-tier footprint. It fits relational database management systems, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, build and deployment servers, and mid-sized data processing pipelines that require predictable processing cycles, generous memory space, and direct fast disk access.
